Taxonomy

Assign taxonomic labels to viral sequences using gene-sharing networks.

Stage 6 of the Viral Metagenome Workflow. Click Taxonomy for the walkthrough, or a neighboring stage to browse its tools.

Taxonomic classification of uncultivated viruses is challenging because most lack close relatives in reference databases. A relatively recent and powerful approach organizes viral sequence space through gene-sharing networks: viruses that share a significant fraction of their protein content are grouped into genus-level clusters benchmarked against ICTV-classified reference genomes. Viruses co-clustering with classified references inherit their taxonomy, with isolated clusters representing putative novel genera. For species-level demarcation, nucleotide-similarity tools like VIRIDIC complement the protein-based network approach.
Tool Description Platforms Links Reference
vConTACT2 Assigns taxonomy to uncultivated prokaryotic viruses using gene-sharing networks benchmarked against the ICTV. HPC CyVerse Docs · Official Bin Jang et al., Nat Biotechnol (2019)
vConTACT2-Gene2Genome Preprocessing step for vConTACT2. Converts protein FASTA sequences into the gene-to-genome mapping file required by the classifier. HPC CyVerse KBase Docs coming soon · Official Bin Jang et al., Nat Biotechnol (2019)
CAT/BAT Taxonomic classification of assembled contigs (CAT) and metagenome-assembled bins (BAT) using DIAMOND-based alignment and a last common ancestor approach. HPC Docs · Official von Meijenfeldt et al., Genome Biol (2019)
VIRIDIC Calculates intergenomic similarity between phage genomes using BLAST-based nucleotide comparisons, enabling genus- and species-level demarcation following ICTV criteria. HPC Docs · Official Moraru et al., Viruses (2020)
vConTACT3 Gene-sharing network classification of viral genomes with hierarchical, multi-rank taxonomic assignment. HPC Docs coming soon · Official Bolduc et al., Nature Biotechnology (2025)
